distinguishing_features: The candidate deliberately promotes heterogeneous nucleation at a selected temperature, whereas Prior Art 1 suppresses it on reactor walls.
The candidate places nucleating sites in a cryovial to control freezing of a cell-containing sample.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce damage associated with variable ice-nucleation onset during cryopreservation.
parsed.viable_reason: Although surface-seeded nucleation is feasible, the stated generic seeds do not establish a reproducible activation temperature, and earlier nucleation does not reduce the latent heat released or demonstrate reduced cellular damage.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Deliberately using heterogeneous nucleation to control freezing is a direct, predictable application of the nucleation physics in Prior Art 1 and a routine response to stochastic supercooling.
